newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific seeks to acquire Pennzoil for $6.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific seeks to acquire Pennzoil for $6.4 billion.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc. said Monday it renewed its attempt to acquire Pennzoil Co., offering a two-step cash and stock transaction valued at about $6.4 billion.
News of the offer, valued at $84 per Pennzoil share, sent the stock soaring in pre-opening trading. It leaped to $85 from its $59.625 finish Friday on the New York Stock Exchange.

Pennzoil management said it would review the offer and promised a response on or before July 7. It asked Pennzoil shareholders to defer taking any action on the Union Pacific tender offer until the company issues its response.

"We believe that the merger of UPR and Pennzoil will create the premier independent exploration and production company in the U.S.," Union Pacific Chairman and Chief Executive Jack Messman said in a statement. "Driven by UPR's proven ability to drill and develop oil and gas properties quickly and efficiently, we are confident that UPR will create growth and value well beyond what Pennzoil can achieve on its own."
Union Pacific said the combined company would lead the industry in a number of performance measures, including drilling activity, production and cash flow.
Union Pacific said the first step would be a cash tender offer for 50.1 percent of Pennzoil's shares, starting Monday, followed by a tax-free exchange of shares for the remaining 49.9 percent.
The company said the deal would offer an immediate and ongoing accretion to its cash flow per share. However, it is expected to have a near-term dilutive effect on earnings per share.
In the second step of the offer, each remaining Pennzoil share will be exchanged for Union Pacific shares.

The transaction must be approved by Union Pacific and Pennzoil shareholders. It is not conditioned upon financing and the cash tender offer will be financed by Union Pacific with bank borrowings, it said.

Union Pacific's Messman sent a letter to Pennzoil Chairman and Chief Executive James Pate, whom the company said in a statement has "repeatedly rebuffed UPR's efforts to have any serious discussion about a possible transaction."
"These two companies belong together," Messman said in the letter.
Messman's letter also mentioned that Pate in 1995 proposed a merger with UPR, when it was a subsidiary of Union Pacific Corp.
Messman's letter also questioned Pate's view, contained in a May 8, 1997, letter to Messman, that a merger somehow no longer made sense, the company said.

"We do not understand," Messman wrote, "why you believed that two years ago, when Pennzoil faced particularly severe problems, it was in a better position than it is now to merge with UPR and form the premier independent E&P (energy and petroleum) company. In fact, we believe that today the benefits from a combination would come even more quickly."
Union Pacific Resources said it sought a friendly merger but that its advances were repeatedly rebuffed.

"Your continued refusal to discuss the rationale or valuation of a transaction has left us with no choice but to present our offer directly to Pennzoil shareholders," Messman wrote. "While we are still prepared to discuss a friendly transaction, the UPR board of directors strongly supports pursuing a business combination now."
